A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DREMA and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–N. Content can be matched reliably despite pagination and wording changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original RLBench and real-robot experiments, transformation ablations, dataset-size analyses, and world-model localization measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the main comparisons and supplementary results in the appendices.

M1.justification: The object-centric Gaussian reconstruction, depth-supervised optimization, PyBullet dynamics, equivariant transformations, and demonstration verification remain unchanged. Appendix G discusses possible future extensions rather than implementing a new component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine RLBench tasks, three-task joint-learning setting, and five real-robot tasks, including the same out-of-distribution configurations. The corrected box-color description in Appendix F matches the photographs already present in v1.

E2.justification: The evaluated PerAct, random-patch, random-table-color, distractor, and Replay comparisons are retained. RVT2 and Diffusion Policy appear in v2 as proposed future evaluations, not additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both versions specify the same training budgets, 40 simulation validation examples, 50 simulation test configurations, and 20 real-world test configurations. Appendix L's revised wording about adjustments in the reconstruction clarifies the documented setup without establishing a changed experimental procedure.

E4.justification: The dataset-size study, transformation ablations, keypoint-coverage analysis, runtime measurements, failure examples, segmentation comparisons, and rendering analyses are retained. Expanded discussion of articulated objects adds no experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same five simulation test runs, mean ± standard deviation and maximum success rates, and Figure 4 error bars. No repeated-run, seed, or statistical-estimation practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4, A.5, and B.6 match, and Figure 4 retains its plotted results. For example, both report single-task averages of 25.1% versus 16.0% and real-robot averages of 62.9% versus 31.7% for DREMA with all data versus PerAct. The qualitative visual evidence is also retained.

T1.justification: The world-model definition, reconstruction loss, dynamics equation, transformation definitions, and verification inequality remain unchanged. Appendix L repeats an existing demonstration definition and harmonizes notation rather than introducing new mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract explicitly reframes the contribution as automatic construction of learnable digital twins bridging digital twins and world models. This promotes a connection already discussed in v1 Appendix E; the central compositionality, imagination-based learning, and one-shot-learning claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix G expands the proposed routes to articulated-object modeling through motion, foundation-model segmentation, and URDF construction. The conclusion additionally identifies evaluation with newer policies and direct RGB-based approaches as future work. Existing applicability limits and result interpretations largely remain.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the project-site address and removes the statement that source code can be found there; both reproducibility statements still promise code and synthetic-data release. Appendices F and L correct the box-color and reconstruction descriptions. These are documentation changes, not evidence of changed resource availability or rerun experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Diffusion Policy reference by Chi et al. and removes the NARF24 reference by Lewis et al.; URDFormer remains cited. Learnable-digital-twin positioning becomes more prominent, while the main related-work comparisons remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and parts of Appendix G are rewritten, with scattered grammatical corrections elsewhere. Appendix L aligns notation with Section 4 and repeats its demonstration-definition paragraph. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from page 3 to page 2, several captions are shortened, Table 4's average-column labels change, and surrounding material reflows. The figure collection and table structures remain substantially intact; all embedded raster images are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the digital-twin interpretation clearer, elaborates concrete extension directions, and corrects task/setup descriptions in Appendices F and L. These provide modest clarity and documentation gains while retaining the scientific evidence. Redundant prose in Appendix L and the less clear Table 1 caption offset some editorial improvement.
